p.src: Now the heroes of Liangshan Marsh had defeated Gao Qiu three times in naval battle and captured him and all his men, bringing them up the mountain. Song Gongming refused to kill them and released every one. Grand Marshal Gao allowed the bulk of his troops to return to the capital, and himself took Xiao Rang and Yue He to the Eastern Capital to await the matter of amnesty, while leaving his adviser Wen Huanzhang at Liangshan Marsh. While at Liangshan Marsh, Gao Qiu had personally declared, “When I return to court, I shall take Xiao Rang and the others before the Son of Heaven, earnestly memorialize and recommend you, and have an envoy sent here at once to offer amnesty.” For that reason, they appointed Yue He to accompany Xiao Rang, and the two departed together. Of this, no more need be said. Meanwhile, the chieftains of Liangshan Marsh held council. Song Jiang said, “Judging by Gao Qiu, I cannot tell whether he will keep his word after leaving here.” Wu Yong laughed. “From what I see, that man has waspish eyes and a serpentine form. He is one who turns his face and forgets every favor. He has lost vast numbers of troops and squandered great stores of the court’s money and grain. Once back in the Eastern Capital, he will surely plead illness and stay out of sight, make some vague report to the Son of Heaven, and temporarily dismiss the soldiers to rest. Xiao Rang and Yue He will be kept under discreet house arrest in his residence. If we wait for amnesty, we shall only waste our strength and worry!” Song Jiang said, “If so, what are we to do? Never mind the amnesty—we have also delivered those two into his hands.” Wu Yong said, “Brother, choose two more sharp-witted men and send them to the Eastern Capital with plenty of gold and treasure to learn what is happening. Let them use gifts to open the necessary doors and make our true sentiments known to His Present Majesty, leaving Grand Marshal Gao no means of concealing the affair. That is our best plan.” Yan Qing rose and said, “Last year, when we caused that disturbance in the Eastern Capital, it was I who gained admittance to Li Shishi’s house. After that great uproar, her household must already have guessed eight parts out of ten. Yet there is one advantage: she is the Son of Heaven’s beloved, and His Majesty has no suspicions of her. She must surely have reported, ‘The men of Liangshan Marsh learned that Your Majesty was traveling there incognito, and so came to frighten you. The matter has already been smoothed over.’ This time I shall take more gold and pearls and use them to gain access there. Influence exerted upon the pillow works fastest of all. I can adapt my stay to circumstances and act as opportunity dictates.” Song Jiang said, “Worthy brother, this journey will place a heavy responsibility upon you!” Dai Zong at once said, “I shall go along to help him.” Zhu Wu, the Resourceful Strategist, said, “Elder brother, when you attacked Huazhou in former days, you once rendered Grand Marshal Su a service. He is a kindhearted man. If we can persuade him to memorialize the Son of Heaven from time to time, the affair should also proceed smoothly.” Song Jiang recalled the words of the Mysterious Maiden of the Ninth Heaven: “When you meet Su, joy shall come again and again.” Could they be fulfilled through this very man? He therefore invited Adviser Wen into the hall to sit with them. Song Jiang asked, “Sir, are you acquainted with Grand Marshal Su Yuanjing?” Wen Huanzhang replied, “He and I were schoolfellows and friends. Nowadays he is never a step away from His Majesty. He is exceedingly benevolent and generous, and in all his dealings with others he is kindness itself.” Song Jiang said, “I shall conceal nothing from you, sir. We suspect that when Grand Marshal Gao returns to the capital, he will not memorialize the matter of our amnesty. When Grand Marshal Su went to Huazhou in former days to offer incense, he and I, Song Jiang, met once. Now we wish to send someone to approach him with gifts and ask him to lend his influence, memorializing the Son of Heaven from time to time so that together we may bring this affair to completion.” Adviser Wen replied, “Since that is your intention, General, I shall write a personal letter for them to deliver.” Song Jiang was delighted. He immediately ordered paper and brushes brought. Meanwhile, he burned fine incense, took out the divination text bestowed by the Mysterious Maiden, prayed toward the heavens, and obtained a supremely auspicious omen. He then laid out a farewell feast for Dai Zong and Yan Qing. They packed gold, pearls, and other valuables into two large hampers, concealed the letter upon themselves, and also carried official documents bearing the seal of Kaifeng Prefecture. Disguised as constables, the two bade farewell to the chieftains and descended the mountain. They crossed Golden Sands Strand and set out for the Eastern Capital.

p.src: Dai Zong carried an umbrella in his hand and a bundle on his back. Yan Qing slung the hampers from his fire-and-water staff, hitched up his black constable’s robe, tied a money pouch around his waist, bound his legs with gaiters and kneepads, and wore cross-strapped hemp sandals. As they traveled, they ate when hungry, drank when thirsty, lodged at night, and journeyed at dawn. After some days they reached the Eastern Capital. Instead of entering by the gate directly on their route, they made a detour to the Gate of Longevity. When the two reached the city gate, the guards barred their way. Yan Qing set down the hampers and, speaking in a rustic accent, demanded, “Why are you stopping me?” The soldier said, “The Palace Commandant’s Office has issued strict orders. For fear that men of every sort from Liangshan Marsh may smuggle themselves into the city, all gates have been instructed to question every out-of-town traveler entering or leaving with the utmost care.” Yan Qing laughed. “A fine constable you are! You keep questioning your own people. The two of us have served in Kaifeng Prefecture since childhood and passed through this gate tens of thousands of times, yet you perversely question us again and again, while men from Liangshan Marsh pass right before your wide-open eyes!” He pulled the forged document from inside his clothes, flung it straight at the man’s face, and said, “Look! Is this an official document from Kaifeng Prefecture or not?” Hearing this, the officer overseeing the gate shouted, “If they have documents from Kaifeng Prefecture, why keep questioning them? Let them in!” Yan Qing snatched back the document, thrust it into his robe, lifted the hampers, and walked on. Dai Zong also gave a derisive chuckle. The two went straight toward Kaifeng Prefecture and found an inn where they settled in.

p.src: The next day, Yan Qing changed into a homespun shirt, tied a sash around his waist, put on a different headscarf and wore it askew, disguising himself as an idle young loafer. He took a kerchief of gold and pearls from the chest and instructed Dai Zong, “Brother, I am going to Li Shishi’s house on business today. If anything goes awry, make haste back by yourself.” Having given Dai Zong his instructions, he set straight out and made directly for Li Shishi’s house. When he reached the gate and looked, he saw the same winding balustrades and carved railings, green-latticed windows and vermilion doors, now refurbished even more splendidly than before. Yan Qing raised the mottled-bamboo blind and turned in by the side entrance, where an exquisite fragrance already filled the air. Entering the reception room, he saw paintings and calligraphy by celebrated masters hanging all around. Beneath the eaves stood twenty or thirty pots of fantastically shaped rocks and ancient pines; the couches were all made of carved, fragrant nanmu wood, and every daybed and cushion was covered in brocade and embroidery. Yan Qing coughed softly. A maid came out and, upon seeing him, went to announce him to Mother Li. When Mother Li emerged and recognized Yan Qing, she started in alarm and said, “Why have you come here again?” Yan Qing said, “Please ask the young lady to come out. I have something to tell her.” Mother Li said, “Last time you brought trouble upon our household and had the house wrecked. If you have something to say, say it now.” Yan Qing said, “I can speak only when the young lady herself comes out.” Li Shishi had been listening behind the window for some time, and now she came around and entered the room. When Yan Qing looked at her, she possessed a singular grace: her face was like a crabapple freshened by morning dew, her slender waist like a willow swaying in the east wind. She seemed every inch a jade maiden from the enchanted gardens, surpassing even the immortal sisters of the moon palace. Li Shishi advanced with dainty steps, lightly gathering her patterned skirt, and entered the reception room. Yan Qing rose, placed the kerchief on the table, first bowed four times to Mother Li, and then twice to Mistress Li, the foremost courtesan. Li Shishi demurred, saying, “There is no need for such ceremony! I am still young and unworthy to receive your bows.” When Yan Qing had finished bowing, he rose and said, “After the fright we caused you before, my companions and I had nowhere to take shelter.” Li Shishi said, “Do not try to deceive me. At first you told me, ‘I am Zhang Xian, and those two are travelers from Shandong.’ Then, at the critical moment, you caused that uproar. Had I not cleverly explained matters to His Majesty, another person’s entire household would have been ruined! He left two lines in his lyric: ‘Six times six the wild geese fly in ranks joined with eight and nine; we wait only for tidings from the golden cock.’ I became suspicious at once and was just about to ask, when His Majesty arrived unexpectedly. Then that disturbance broke out, and I never had the chance to ask. I am glad you have come today. Now set my doubts at rest. Conceal nothing, but tell me the whole truth. Unless you speak plainly, I shall certainly not let the matter rest!” Yan Qing said, “I shall tell you the truth from my heart. My lady, queen of flowers, please do not be alarmed! The short, dark man who came last time and sat in the chief seat was none other than Song Jiang, known as ‘Protector of Justice.’ The handsome, fair-faced man seated second, with the trim three-pointed beard, was Chai Jin, called the ‘Little Whirlwind,’ a direct descendant of Emperor Shizong of Later Zhou. The man dressed as a constable who stood before you was Dai Zong, the ‘Magic Messenger.’ The man who fought with Grand Commandant Yang at the gate was none other than Li Kui, the ‘Black Whirlwind.’ As for me, I am a native of Daming Prefecture in Beijing, and everyone calls me Yan Qing, the ‘Prodigal.’ When my brother first came to the Eastern Capital seeking an audience with you, he had me pose as Zhang Xian and enter your household as an attendant. My brother wished to see you not to purchase smiles or seek pleasure, but because he had long heard that you enjoyed the favor of the present emperor. He therefore came in person to lay bare his heart, hoping that you might convey to the imperial hearing our purpose of carrying out Heaven’s justice, safeguarding the realm, and bringing peace to the people, so that we might soon receive amnesty and spare the common people further suffering. If you would grant us this favor, you would be the benefactress of all the tens of thousands at Liangshan Marsh!”

p.src: Now treacherous ministers control the court, slanderous sycophants monopolize power, the path of the worthy is barred, and the plight of those below cannot reach the throne. That is why we sought this avenue of approach; we never meant to alarm you, my lady. My elder brother has nothing worthy to present you, only these few trifles here. We earnestly hope you will graciously accept them.” Yan Qing opened the kerchief and spread it upon the table; it contained gold, pearls, jewels, and precious vessels. The old procuress loved wealth, and the sight of it delighted her; she hurriedly ordered the nurse to put everything away. She then invited Yan Qing into a small inner chamber, seated him, and had fine dishes, tea, and fruit prepared, attending him with great solicitude. As it happened, the emperor visited Li Shishi's house from time to time; therefore, what prince, nobleman, or wealthy young lord would dare come to her house even to ask for a cup of tea? Now dishes, wine, and fruit were set out, and Li Shishi waited upon him in person. Yan Qing said, “I am a man who deserves death. How could I dare sit as an equal before the Lady Queen of Flowers?” Li Shishi said, “Do not speak so! I have long heard the great fame of you righteous heroes. It is only because there has been no good man to intercede and help you that you have been left to languish in the marsh stronghold.” Yan Qing said, “When Grand Commandant Chen first came to offer amnesty, the imperial edict contained not a word of pardon or consolation, and even the imperial wine had been secretly replaced. The second time an edict was brought to offer amnesty, they deliberately broke the phrasing at the crucial words and read: ‘Except for Song Jiang, Lu Junyi, and the others, all persons great and small shall be pardoned for the offenses and crimes they have committed.’ For that reason, we did not submit then either. Privy Councillor Tong led his generals against us, but in only two battles they were slaughtered so utterly that not a scrap of armor returned. Afterward, Grand Commandant Gao conscripted laborers from throughout the realm to build ships for another campaign; in just three battles, more than half his men and horses were lost. Grand Commandant Gao was captured alive and taken up the mountain by my elder brother, who refused to harm him, treated him with the utmost courtesy, and sent him back to the capital; all the other captives were likewise released. At Liangshan Marsh he swore a solemn oath that once he returned to court, he would report to the Son of Heaven and immediately arrange our amnesty. He therefore took two men from Liangshan Marsh with him—one was the scholar Xiao Rang, and the other was Yue He, an accomplished singer. Plainly, he has hidden both men in his residence and refuses to let them out. Having lost so many soldiers and generals, he must be concealing it all from the emperor.” Li Shishi said, “After squandering so much money and grain and losing so many troops and generals, how would he dare report it? I understand the whole matter now. For now, drink a few cups, and afterward we shall discuss what is to be done.” Yan Qing said, “By nature, I cannot drink wine.” Li Shishi said, “You have come so far through wind and frost. Now that you are here, relax and drink a few cups.” Unable to withstand her urging, Yan Qing had no choice but to attend her over a cup or two. Now Li Shishi was a courtesan of the pleasure quarters, fickle in affection; seeing Yan Qing's handsome bearing, his ready speech, and his quick, eloquent tongue, she took a fancy to him. During the feast, she made teasing remarks to entice him. After several cups, she began flirting with him through hints and half-spoken phrases. Yan Qing was clever and perceptive in every way; how could he fail to understand? But he had the heart of a true hero and feared jeopardizing his elder brother's great undertaking; how could he dare respond to her advances? Li Shishi said, “I have long heard, elder brother, that you are skilled in all manner of music. It would be a pleasure to hear something as we sit over our wine.” Yan Qing replied, “I have learned a few small arts, but how could I dare display them before you, my lady?” Li Shishi said, “Then I shall play a tune first for you to hear!” She called for a maid to bring her flute. The phoenix flute was drawn from its brocade case. Li Shishi took it and blew softly into it, producing sounds that truly seemed to pierce the clouds and split stone. Yan Qing listened and applauded without cease. When Li Shishi had finished the tune, she passed the flute to Yan Qing and said, “Elder brother, play a tune for me as well!” Yan Qing wished to please the woman, so he had no choice but to display his skill. Taking the flute, he too played a plaintive, sobbing tune.

p.src: From outside, I shall toss two ropes over the wall. Fasten them securely to the nearest willow tree. The two of us outside will each hold one rope taut, and you two can climb along them and get out. We shall do it at the fourth watch. Do not miss the appointed time.” The officer then said, “What are you two still talking about? Be off with you!” Yue He went back inside and secretly informed Xiao Rang. Yan Qing hurried back and told Dai Zong. They waited until nightfall that very day. Now Yan Qing and Dai Zong bought two stout ropes in the street and concealed them about their persons. They first went behind Grand Commandant Gao’s residence to survey where they might take position. It happened that a river ran behind the residence, and two empty boats were moored near the bank. The two hid inside an empty boat. When at last they heard the watch drum sound the fourth watch, they came ashore, circled behind the wall, and coughed. A cough answered from within. Both sides understood the signal, and Yan Qing tossed the ropes over the wall. Judging that the ropes had been firmly secured within, the two braced themselves outside, each pulling against the other and gripping the rope ends tightly. Yue He climbed out first, followed by Xiao Rang. Both slid down, then threw the ropes back inside the wall.
